2016_095_060716mtg.paragraph: Agenda and full board packet for the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education held June 7, 2016, at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. Most of the packet is a student recognition block lettered A through OOO, but it also carries four personnel actions, two business items and a bond construction report. The most consequential action is the property/casualty/liability insurance award: the Board is asked to accept the MASB-SEG Property/Casualty Pool proposal effective July 1, 2016 for an amount not to exceed $276,715.00, moving the district off the MAISL pool, which quoted $309,557.00.

**Meeting**

Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, June 7, 2016, 7:00 p.m., Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. The masthead gives the district address as 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, and notes meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Order of business: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication; General - Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda); Other; Adjournment.

**Recognition (A through OOO)**

Item A honors Assistant Superintendent Rick L. West as 2015-16 Oakland County School Business Administrator of the Year; he was nominated by Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky, Trustee Gary Hauff spoke at the ceremony, and OCSBO President Tina Kostiuk was invited to present. The remaining items cover All-State Winter athletes, Senior Scholar Athletes at a 3.5 grade point average, MSBOA All-State Band, Honors Band and Orchestra, and scores of academic competitions. Reader assignments rotate among Nancy Philippart, Mike Jolly, Karl Schmidt, Paula Fleming, Ida Edmunds, Gary Hauff, Todd Miletti and Wendy Underwood; the recommended action throughout is to congratulate students and distribute pins.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**

Minutes of the May 3, 2016 Special Meeting and Closed Session, the May 3, 2016 Workshop, the May 17, 2016 Special Meeting and the May 17, 2016 Board Meeting. The May 3 special meeting adopted resolution 16-037 selecting D.M. Burr Group for custodial, grounds and warehouse services under an RFP issued March 14, 2016 (Yes 7, No 0), then went into closed session on attorney-client privilege under Public Act 267, Section 8(c). The May 17 regular meeting adopted a Teacher Appreciation Week resolution, ratified two three-year support-staff agreements, approved a copier lease at an annual cost not to exceed $73,374.72, and designated Todd Miletti to cast the district's Oakland Schools ballot.

**Personnel (item 6)**

| Action | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| TEA contract ratification | Tentative agreement reached May 25, 2016 with the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA; TEA membership ratified June 6, 2016; term July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2017 |
| New hire | Stephanie Pilarski, 1.0 Teacher, Bemis Elementary School, probationary contract for 2016-2017 |
| Assistant Principal, Athens High School | Dan Mills, interim since December 2015; two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective July 1, 2016 |
| Principal, Troy Union Elementary | Michael Cottone, interim since November 2015; two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective July 1, 2016 |

**Business (item 8)**

Item A sets a public hearing on the proposed 2016-2017 budget for June 21, 2016 at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice published at least six days in advance and copies available at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 15, 2016 through Tuesday, June 21, 2016.

Item B awards property/casualty/liability insurance. Rick West's May 25, 2016 memo to Dr. Rich Machesky compares the two pools:

| Pool | Total premium |
| --- | --- |
| SET SEG (MASB-SEG Property Casualty Pool) | $276,715.00 |
| MAISL | $309,557.00 |

West states the SET SEG program adds SafeSchools online training, premises medical payments for students and a property appraisal service valued in combination at $45,000 at no additional cost, and that changing providers will save Troy School District $32,842. He notes the MAISL Pool has 33 members, four of which including Troy solicited bids this year, and that SET SEG covers over 500 public schools statewide.

**Other (item 10)**

Rick West presents a 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update for June 2016 prepared with Barton Malow and TMP, covering the Troy High chiller and pool dehumidification work, Athens mechanical room upgrades and boiler demolition, gymnasium lighting at both high schools, and the International Academy East locker-room-to-classroom conversion. No action is required.
2016_095_060716mtg.verbose:
Board meeting agenda and packet for the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education on June 7, 2016, at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School, 4333 John R, Troy, MI 48085. The cover sheet lists the district address as 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, states that meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and points viewers to http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

RECOGNITION. Item 2.A, read by Nancy Philippart, recognizes Assistant Superintendent Rick L. West as the 2015-16 Oakland County School Business Administrator of the Year. West was nominated by Superintendent Dr. Rich Machesky with support from the Board and central office staff; Trustee Gary Hauff spoke on the Board's behalf at the ceremony; OCSBO President Tina Kostiuk was invited to present. West is an active member of the Michigan School Business Officials (MSBO), an MSBO Leadership Institute participant, and past president of OCSBO.

Item 2.B, read by Mike Jolly, lists All-State Athletes for Winter 2016, dominated by Troy High synchronized swimmers (Monica Alluri, Ellen Barker, Michelle Cai, Inwoo Cho, Seungwon (Hanna) Jung, Soumeeka Koneru, Kaylee Lee, Julia Meng, Anjali Munasinghe, Sabina Ravindran, Bhavya Sukhavasi, Amishi Taneja, Anishka Taneja, Rohini Verma, Christina Xu, Serena Yee, Kathleen Young) with Camille Bedford and Kathleen Ward of Athens, Maxwell Chen in boys swimming, Emily Morgan in figure skating and Griffin Olis in boys diving. Item 2.C lists the 2015-2016 Senior Scholar Athletes at a 3.5 grade point average from Athens HS and Troy HS.

Items 2.D through 2.OOO recognize academic and arts competitions, each recommending the Board congratulate students and distribute pins. Figures as printed include: All-State Orchestra (Boulan Park), where an average of over 2,000 students audition each year for the 400 seats in five ensembles; the American Mathematics Competitions, more than 60 years old with more than 350,000 students; the College for Creative Studies competition, with nearly 6,000 individual entries and more than 300 senior portfolios in 15 categories, of which 1,093 individual works and 90 portfolios received awards; Destination Imagination Global Finals, drawing over 1,100 teams from 45 states, 7 Canadian provinces and 13 countries and over 15,000 attendees, with Bemis, Wattles and International Academy East first in the state; the Destination Imagination European Invitational in Wroclaw, Poland in April 2016, where a Larson Middle School team was one of only two United States teams among approximately 200 Poland teams and won the Improv challenge with a Top 10 score across 250 teams; HOSA's state competition April 14th-15th in Traverse City with a record 2500 competitors; the 23rd annual Japanese Quiz Bowl at Eastern Michigan University, where 26 Athens students on eight teams brought home five trophies; the Michigan Council of Women in Technology website design competition, in which 816 girls have participated; the Michigan Elementary/Primary Team Chess K-3 Championships in Lansing on March 26th, where twelve teams played five rounds and the Barnard team won the Primary K-3C category; the Math Kangaroo Olympiad of March 19th, given in 38 U.S. states with 21,000 American students and over 6,000,000 worldwide; the National "Who Wants to be a Mathematician" competition of January 7th in Seattle, where an IAE student took an award of $5000 with a further $5000 to IAE and headed to Hong Kong for the International Mathematical Olympiad, July 6th-16th; Quiz Bowl/America Answers, where Boulan Park scored 1342 out of 1500 for 1st place in the Great Lake State Competition and then answered 99 of 100 questions for a score of 1338, 4th in the Nation; the Scholastic Art and Writing Awards, running since 1923, with 320,000 entries and a Carnegie Hall ceremony June 2nd; Science Olympiad's 23 events, with Baker and Troy High first in the state in Food Science, Chemistry Lab, Dynamic Planet, Experimental Design, Geologic Mapping and Green Generation; a Smith Middle School student who won the Oakland County Spelling Bee on "submersible" and placed 11th in the nation at the Scripps National Spelling Bee on May 22nd; Walsh College's "Make It Better" competition, where 9 of 200 statewide entries came from the Troy High Entrepreneurship Club and 3 of those 9 placed; and the U.S. Chess Federation National Elementary Championships of May 6th-8th in Nashville, where 328 students on 59 teams competed in the "under 800" section and the Barnard team placed 2nd. Further recognitions cover MSBOA All-State Band (Baker, Boulan, Larson) and Honors Band (Smith), the American Nuclear Society art contest, the Brain Bee State Champion, the Chinese Bridge Contest and Chinese Zodiac Art Contest, CSPAN StudentCam, DECA, First Lego League, FIRST Robotics, Future Problem Solving, the Jackie Robinson contest sponsored by the Detroit Tigers for 20 years, JSHS at Wayne State, Marriott Hotels Young Filmmaker of the Year, MIT Inspire, MATHCOUNTS, a Math Olympiad honoree named a 2016 USAMO winner in the top 12, three student Emmy Awards, the Michigan China Quiz Bowl, Michigan Green Schools "Evergreen" status for Athens, MIFA, MIPA, the Michigan Student Film Festival's first John Prusak Visionary Award, Model UN, the National Chemistry Olympiad, the National French and German exams, the Orchard Lake Film Festival, Purple Comet Math, the Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit at Cobo Hall, the Siemens Competition, the Stock Market Game, Toshiba ExploraVision, USA Biology Olympiad, the Verizon Innovative App Challenge and the WordMasters Challenge.

CONSENT AGENDA (item 5). May 3, 2016 Special Meeting, Administration Building: President Philippart called the meeting to order at 5:31 p.m. with Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, administrators Machesky, Carson, Dziatczak, Griffor, Pass and West in attendance, and Mr. Allen from D.M. Burr Group the only member of the audience. Resolution 16-037, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, recites the Request for Proposals for Custodial, Grounds and Warehouse Services issued March 14, 2016 and selects D.M. Burr Group, authorizing the Superintendent or designee to negotiate and execute the contract subject to legal counsel review; Yes 7, No 0, certified under the Open Meeting Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Resolution 16-038 then took the Board into closed session on attorney-client privilege under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) on a unanimous roll call; closed session began 5:51 p.m., the meeting reconvened at 5:54 p.m. and adjourned at 6:52 p.m. The May 3, 2016 Board Workshop (reproduced twice in the packet) was called to order at 6:59 p.m. with administrators Machesky, Dziatczak, Griffor, Young and West and approximately 5 other audience members; it covered a Copier Lease Review and a Teaching & Learning goals update and book club discussion, adjourning at 10:04 p.m. The May 17, 2016 Special Meeting was called to order by Vice-President Schmidt at 6:47 p.m. with Philippart absent and 25 audience members, to discuss the Oakland Schools Board of Education Biennial Election of Monday, June 6th; two individuals filed for the two open seats, both incumbents running unopposed. Adjourned 6:50 p.m.

May 17, 2016 Board Meeting, Services Building: Vice-President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Underwood present, Philippart absent, Superintendent Machesky and administrators Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris and West present, and approximately 150 audience members. A TSD Mission Moment honored Baker Middle School Shark Tank winners guided by teachers Anne Costello, Lisa Gaglio and Colin Quinn, presenting the products "Marshmallow Surprise" and "Shine." The Outstanding Support Staff recognition, described as thirteen individuals nominated, named among others Ann Asmar, Mike Boussie, Pam Brubaker, Shelley Chronowski, Vera Dorr, Gloria Hoffman, Lois Hurdle, Mary Klotz, Jill Martens, Tina Matar, Barb McCoy, Cheryl Moder, Candy Parker, Keith Rehbine, Stacey Schoenherr, Sandra Sinnaeve, Debbie Taylor and Craig Matthes, Classroom Aide/Manager of the Terrace Cafe at Athens High School, who was named Outstanding Support Staff Employee of the Year and forwarded to the county for the Betty Campion Award. Retirees recognized included Faith Clay, Carol Cooper, Valerie Daughtery, Janice Davies, Barbara Davis, Mary Fairweather, Cathy Goergen, Bettie Goss, Steven Gottlieb, Dolores Gould, Nicholas Jabe, Michael Lalko, Anne Lenihan, Terese Libby, Linda McCatty, James McCauley, William Moroski, Sandra Osaer, Janette Przytakoski, Jeanine Sikora, Gayle Spiteri and Karen Waynick, each presented with a certificate and retirement gift. Resolution 16-038 supported National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 2-6, 2016 (Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart). Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence President Al Robinson was recognized; the Foundation funded 79 grants this year. Resolution 16-039 approved minutes of the April 12 and April 19, 2016 meetings, the Treasurer's Report for March 2016, and the Oakland Intermediate School District Budget. Resolution 16-040 ratified the April 26, 2016 tentative agreement with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2019; resolution 16-041 ratified the April 27, 2016 tentative agreement with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA for the same term. Resolution 16-042 authorized a Master Equipment Lease Agreement with Great America Financial Services for a copier fleet for no more than four (4) years at an annual cost not to exceed $73,374.72 per year, plus a Cost per Copy Maintenance Agreement with Applied Imaging not to exceed $.0032 per impression for Canon Monochrome Equipment and $.0049 (black) and .059 (color) per impression for Canon Color Equipment, as General Fund expenditures. Resolution 16-043, under Public Act 419 of 2004, designated Todd Miletti as the Board's representative to the 2016 electoral body, supported candidates Mrs. Barbara DeMarco and Mr. Connie R. Williams for two (2) positions each for a term of six (6) years ending June 30, 2022, and directed Miletti to vote for DeMarco at least on the first ballot on June 6. All these votes were Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Student representatives Parker Gilchrist (Niles Community High School, reporting nearly 50% of graduates finishing with at least one Dual Enrollment college class), Maxwell Fanroy (Athens), Snigdha Suvarna (Troy High) and Victoria Malkoun (International Academy-East, noting graduation May 26th at the Detroit Opera House) gave reports. Adjourned 8:18 p.m. Minutes are submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

PERSONNEL (item 6). 6.A seeks ratification of a tentative agreement reached May 25, 2016 between the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA, ratified by TEA membership on June 6, 2016, covering July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2017 and signed May 25, 2016 by TEA President Tony Lucchi and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services. 6.B recommends a probationary contract for new hire Stephanie Pilarski, 1.0 Teacher, Bemis Elementary School, for 2016-2017. 6.C recommends Mr. Dan Mills as Assistant Principal at Athens High School under a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective July 1, 2016; Mills has been interim assistant principal since December 2015 and since 2007 taught in the Athens English department as chair and AP English instructor, with adjunct work at Oakland Community College and the University of Phoenix, a Michigan State University Bachelor's in English, an Oakland University Master of Arts in English, and enrollment in Oakland University's Education Specialist program with anticipated graduation in August 2016. Supporting material includes his Oakland Human Resources Consortium application (AppNo 157247, submitted 4/27/2016; 5274 Whipple Lake Rd, Clarkston, MI 48348), an April 1, 2016 letter of interest, a March 28, 2016 recommendation from Principal Lara J. Dixon, Ed.D. citing nine years together, a recommendation from Assistant Principal William Turner noting Mills replaced a senior administrator with 29 years of experience who retired mid-year, a resume covering Carver High School in Winston-Salem, NC (Feb. 2005-Jan. 2007), the AppliTrack applicant roster numbered through entry 242 with Daniel Mills at entry 223, and the April 21, 2016 first-round interview schedule on which Mills interviewed at 10:05 a.m.

6.D recommends Mr. Michael Cottone as principal of Troy Union Elementary under a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure effective July 1, 2016; Cottone has been interim principal since November 2015 and taught 3rd, 4th and 5th grades at Bemis Elementary for the last 12 years, holding an Oakland University Bachelor's in Elementary Education and Master's in Educational Leadership. His application (AppNo 137746, submitted 3/15/2016; 3388 West York Court, Rochester Hills, MI 48306) lists Troy Union interim principal 11/2015-06/2016 at a last annual salary of $86,428 and Bemis teacher 08/2004-10/2015 at a last annual salary of $82,428, an undergraduate GPA of 3.44/4 and graduate GPA of 3.92/4, certificate IF0000000233751 expiring 06/30/2017, and tenure in Troy in 2008. References include David Pass, Jeremey Whan, Matt Jansen, Cathy Kochanski, Mark Dziatczak, Jennifer Gottlieb and Tim Fulcher. His portfolio sets Continuous School Improvement goals: proficiency in "structure" in Informational Writing by 6/1/2019 on the Writing Pathways Assessment, Algebraic Thinking proficiency by 6/1/2017 on the Troy Union Grade Level Common Assessment, and grades 3-5 proficiency on the Troy Union Claim/Evidence Assessment by 6/1/2018. The packet includes the AppliTrack roster numbered through entry 133 with Cottone at entry 96, and a June 1, 2016 email from Jordan Harris to Judy Holmes listing first-round interviews (Denis Metty, Derek Adams, Christine Santer, Patricia Wilcox, Julie Alspach, Jerry Jait, Randy Groya, Denye Griessel, Mike Cottone, Michelle Barsh, John Pagel), second round (Cottone, Barsh, Metty, Pagel) and third round (Cottone, Pagel).

BUSINESS (item 8). 8.A resolves to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2016-2017 budget on June 21, 2016 at 7:00 p.m. at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice published at least six (6) days beforehand including, in 11-point bold faced type, the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing. Exhibit A states copies will be available at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., Wednesday, June 15, 2016 through Tuesday, June 21, 2016, over the signature of Paula Fleming.

8.B awards property/casualty/liability insurance for 2016/2017. Proposals were solicited from the MAISL Insurance Pool and the MASB-SEG Property/Casualty Pool; the resolution accepts the MASB-SEG proposal effective July 1, 2016 for an amount not to exceed $276,715.00. Rick West's May 25, 2016 memorandum to Dr. Rich Machesky (Business Office, 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4022) reports quoted total premiums of $276,715.00 from SET SEG and $309,557.00 from MAISL, notes the SET SEG program adds SafeSchools online training, premises medical payments for students and a property appraisal service valued in combination at $45,000 at no additional cost, and states changing providers will save Troy School District $32,842. The MAISL Pool has 33 members, four including Troy soliciting bids this year, two of the other three confirming they will recommend leaving; SET SEG covers over 500 public schools in the state. The attached comparison exhibits carry a mismatched template header reading "July 1, 2013-2014 Coverage Comparison Elida Local Schools" and show building and contents coverage of $76,246,300 versus $367,857,460, flood and earthquake limits of $25,000,000 with $1,000 deductibles versus $2,000,000 and $1,000,000, boiler and machinery limits of $250,000,000 versus $100,000,000, a commercial blanket bond of $1,500,000 versus $1,000,000, school board legal liability (carrier MCRMT) of $1,000,000 per claim with a $12,500 deductible versus $10,000,000 with a $10,000 deductible, and excess liability of $10,000,000 under both.

OTHER (item 10). Rick West presents the Troy School District 2013 Bond Program Series 1 Construction Update for June 2016, prepared by Barton Malow and TMP, illustrated with the Troy High chiller installation and pool dehumidification upgrades, Athens mechanical room upgrades and boiler demolition, gymnasium lighting upgrades at both high schools, and the International Academy East locker room to classroom conversion. Completed 2015 projects are BP#5 (Troy High Areas F & G band/theatre addition and remodel and Area J classroom addition), BP#6 (Boulan Park and Larson office additions), BP#9 (Boulan Park and Larson mechanical and electrical upgrades), BP#13 (Niles toilet room renovations and Smith Middle School gym and locker room renovations) and BP#14 (Administration and Services Building roofing). 2016 projects are BP#8 (Athens mechanical and electrical upgrades; Troy High pool dehumidification, gym lights and chiller replacement), BP#16 (IAE locker room conversion plus mechanical and electrical upgrades, and Hamilton Elementary mechanical and electrical upgrades) and BP#17 (site work and site lighting at Athens and Troy High Schools, Smith Middle School and Schroeder Elementary). Spring 2016 roofing includes a restoration package reported 80% complete covering 15 buildings plus the completed Troy High pool area; summer 2016 roofing covers Bemis, Costello, Hill and Wass Elementary Schools and Athens High School; painting covers Leonard Elementary, Morse Elementary and Troy High School; and projects in design include mechanical and electrical upgrades at Barnard, Bemis and Wass Elementary Schools and an exterior door replacement project at Troy High and Athens. The report requires no action.
